newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi admits taxes risen 1.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi admits taxes risen 1.1 pct.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday that taxes had risen 1.1 percent under his centre-left government, but the bitter budgetary medicine he was doling out in a bid to join European monetary union was working.

Prodi told a current affairs show on state television RAI he hoped taxes could be reduced by five to six percentage points in future, but added that would be impossible until a clean-up of state finances was complete and recovery underway.
"Ladies and gentlemen, do we want to clean up this country or not?" Prodi asked.

"The objective is to reduce the fiscal pressure by five to six percentage points, but first we have to clean up state finances...If we hadn't taken the steps this government has, the country would have been ruined."
Prodi has introduced just under 100 trillion lire of belt- tightening since taking office in May 1996.
"That's much more than I thought because the accounts were worse than I thought," Prodi said.

But he repeated his conviction that the ratio of Italy's deficit to gross domestic product would hit the three percent target required by the Maaastricht Treaty, which sets the qualifying terms to join monetary union in 1999.
Prodi said that on taking office, he had forecast 18 tough months ahead. But he saw signs of recovery already and thought there may be less pain ahead than he had at first forecast.
"We'll know in a month or two," he added.
